title: Cohort exposure and test history for the cohorts of Fig. 5
legend: **Extended Data Table 1 | Cohort exposure and test history for the cohorts of Fig. 5.** AI-READI is the development cohort, scored out of fold, and eICU is a training source listed to show what encoder exposure means. INSPIRE, HiRID and KNHANES 2022 to 2023 never trained the encoder but were scored before with an earlier checkpoint, so none is untouched validation. KNHANES 2024 was evaluated once as a locked temporal test. Every readout was fitted on the 10,620 KNHANES 2022 to 2023 adults aged 19 to 79 and locked (fit lock 47113a35) before any 2024 row was decoded, and the encoder was not refitted. No external cohort has retinal images, so external rows test the missing-input route and cannot test fusion. Counts with ≥ are released lower bounds rounded down to 20, fold 0 continuation exposure or INSPIRE test-split survivors, and are not additive. KNHANES counts are rounded down to 10 by their release, and the KNHANES 2022 to 2023 count is the fitting set, not the earlier evaluation. With the earlier checkpoint BRAN trailed raw-input readouts in 5, tied in 1 and led in 1 of 7 KNHANES 2022 to 2023 comparisons, and the support of that evaluation is PLACEHOLDER. The HiRID admission count is suppressed by its source and is PLACEHOLDER. Every cell was asserted against a phrase in a named source at build time (Source Data).

disclosure: Counts are of three kinds, as people_count_type states. AI-READI is exact, counts printed with ≥ are released lower bounds rounded down to a multiple of 20, and KNHANES counts are rounded down to a multiple of 10 by their release. The HiRID admission count is withheld. No cell below 20 and no per-person value is present.
